mainTopic: Why the משנה counts 'two ways' (excluding חליצה), and the source that קידושין works with כסף and that a daughter's קידושין money goes to her father
overview: The amud opens with the end of an earlier answer: a woman will not give herself over for less than a פרוטה, so חליפין is not a way of קידושין. Next the גמרא says the 'two ways' a woman goes free exclude חליצה, and proves from 'ספר כריתות' that only a document cuts a marriage. Then a new section asks for the source that a woman is acquired with כסף, and that a daughter's קידושין money belongs to her father. רב יהודה in the name of רב learns both from 'ויצאה חנם אין כסף': money goes to another master, the father. The גמרא asks why the money should not go to the girl herself, especially a נערה, and answers with 'בנעוריה בית אביה'. But רב הונא's separate source for a daughter's earnings shows that this פסוק is only about vows. Vows, fines, and בושת ופגם all fail as sources for money law. So the גמרא returns to 'יצאה חנם אין כסף' and begins a logical argument that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A woman does not give herself over so cheaply
steps.stepSummary: These are the closing words of the earlier answer: a woman does not let herself be acquired for less than a פרוטה, so חליפין cannot be a way of קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: …she does not let herself be acquired [for something so small].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from the previous discussion. A woman would not agree to be acquired for something worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא explained that the number 'three' in the first half of the משנה excludes חליפין. חליפין can work even with an item worth less than a פרוטה. A woman, however, does not give herself over for so little, so חליפין is not a way to marry a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: she transfers ownership / lets herself be acquired
herself
acquisition by exchanging an item (the case being ruled out here)

phrases.english: does not render herself acquired.
phrases.notes: This ends the earlier answer: a woman won't give herself over for less than a פרוטה, so חליפין doesn't work for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous part of the daf, explaining why חליפין is excluded by the number in the רישא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical distinction about the woman's attitude
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חליפין might work for קידושין, the same way it works for buying property.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman does not let herself be acquired for less than a פרוטה, so חליפין is excluded.

steps.title: What does the number in the second half exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the number 'two' in the סיפא ('she acquires herself in two ways') comes to rule out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the latter clause, what does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the second half of the משנה, which says a woman goes free in 'two ways' (a גט or the husband's death). It asks what that number is meant to leave out. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a number in a משנה is never extra; it must be excluding something. It already asked this about the 'three' in the first half. Now it asks the same about the 'two' in the second half.

keyTerms.meaning: the number / the count
the latter clause of the משנה
to exclude

phrases.english: The number in the latter clause
phrases.notes: He means 'האשה קונה את עצמה בשתי דרכים': she goes free in two ways.

phrases.english: serves to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the number in the רישא, the גמרא asks the same question about the number in the סיפא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case is ruled out by the number 'two' in the סיפא?

steps.title: It excludes חליצה, which a קל וחומר might have suggested
steps.stepSummary: The number excludes חליצה. Without it, we might have reasoned with a קל וחומר from a יבמה that a married woman can also be freed by חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It excludes חליצה. You might have thought: let it be learned by a קל וחומר from a יבמה. A יבמה cannot be freed with a גט, yet she is freed with חליצה. So this married woman, who can be freed with a גט, should surely be freed with חליצה! The count teaches us that she cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'two ways' rule out חליצה. It explains why we might have thought חליצה works for a married woman, and says the משנה's count teaches us otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this. A יבמה is 'harder' to release, since a גט does not free her, yet חליצה does. A married woman is 'easier' to release, since a גט does free her, so חליצה should surely work too. The משנה limits the ways to two in order to block this reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: the ceremony that frees a יבמה from the brother-in-law
you might have thought to say
an argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
a widow bound to her late husband's brother
it teaches us (that this is not so)

steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר is NOT the conclusion. It is the mistaken 'might have thought' (הוה אמינא) that the משנה's number comes to reject.

phrases.english: To exclude חליצה.
It would enter your mind to say:
let it be derived by a קל וחומר from a יבמה,
just as a יבמה, who is not released by a גט,
is released by חליצה,
this one, who is released by a גט,
is it not logical that she is released by חליצה?
It teaches us [that she is not].

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number excludes חליצה, which a קל וחומר from יבמה might otherwise have allowed for a married woman.

steps.title: Maybe the קל וחומר is actually correct
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why not accept the קל וחומר and say חליצה really does free a married woman?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe the קל וחומר is right, and a married woman really can go free through חליצה. This challenge sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is a strong תורה-level argument. A count in a משנה alone seems too weak to override it. So the גמרא demands a real source showing why the קל וחומר fails.

keyTerms.meaning: but say it is indeed so

phrases.english: And say that it is indeed so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection of the קל וחומר in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה's count excludes חליצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר looks logically sound, so why should we reject it?

steps.title: Only a written document cuts the marriage
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'ספר כריתות': a document cuts her off, and nothing else does. So חליצה cannot end a marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'a scroll of severance': a scroll cuts her off, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. Only a written document (a גט) can end a marriage while the husband is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ספר' tells us the cutting off must come through a written document. That rules out any other method, including חליצה. A פסוק overrides a קל וחומר, so the קל וחומר falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: a scroll of severance (a גט)
cuts her off / severs her

steps.whatToRemember: The 'two ways' in the משנה exclude חליצה. A married woman goes free only with a גט (or the husband's death), because the פסוק 'ספר כריתות' says only a document cuts the bond.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'A scroll of severance',
a scroll severs her,
and nothing else severs her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation overrides the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A married woman could be freed by חליצה because of the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a document severs a marriage, so חליצה does not work.

steps.title: What is the source for קידושין with כסף?
steps.stepSummary: A new section begins on the משנה's word 'בכסף'. Where do we learn that a woman can be acquired with money?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With money.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the first way of קידושין listed in the משנה, money, and asks for its source. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was explaining the numbers in the משנה. Now it starts going through each method one by one, beginning with כסף, and asks for the source in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: with money
from where do we know?

phrases.english: With money. From where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic: the source for each method of קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for קידושין through money.

steps.title: And why does the money go to her father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second question based on another משנה: the father controls his daughter's קידושין. Where do we learn that money works, and that the money belongs to the father?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, about what we learned: 'A father has authority over his daughter for her קידושין, through money, a document, or intercourse.' From where do we know that she is acquired with money, and that the money is her father's?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second question to the first. It quotes a משנה saying a father controls his young daughter's קידושין. It asks for the source that money works, and that the money goes to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here. First, the source that money creates קידושין, which is the same as Step 6. Second, a new point: the source that when a daughter is married off with money, the money belongs to her father. The גמרא wants one answer that covers both.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore
that which we learned in a משנה
has the right / authority
a document
intercourse

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which we learned:
'A father has authority over his daughter in her betrothal,'
'through money, through a document, and through intercourse,'
from where do we derive that she is acquired with money,
and that the money is her father's?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ הָא דִּתְנַן הָאָב זַכַּאי בְּבִתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second question to Step 6, about who receives the קידושין money.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that money creates קידושין, and that the money for a daughter's קידושין belongs to her father.

steps.title: The money goes to the father, learned from 'without money'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the פסוק 'ויצאה חנם אין כסף' teaches that no money goes to this master, but money does go to another master, the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the פסוק says 'And she shall go out for free, without money.' That means no money goes to this master, but money does go to a different master. Who is that? The father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 7: where do we learn that money works for קידושין, and that the money belongs to the father?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about an אמה עבריה (Jewish maidservant) who goes free from her master without paying him anything. The extra words 'אין כסף' suggest a contrast: when she leaves a different 'master', her father, money is paid. That happens when she leaves her father's authority through קידושין, so the money is his.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant
For free, without payment
Master; someone who has authority over her
Father

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is not about marriage at all. It is about a maidservant going free. The גמרא reads the extra words 'אין כסף' as a hint about a different 'master', the father, who does get money when she leaves him through קידושין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one derivation teaches two things together: money can create קידושין, and a young girl's קידושין money belongs to her father.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
For the verse says: "And she shall go out for free, without money"
phrases.notes: שמות 21:11. This is about a Jewish maidservant who goes free when she grows up.

phrases.english: there is no money for this master,
but there is money for a different master.
And who is that? The father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words 'אין כסף' (שמות 21:11) show that money is paid to the father when she leaves his authority, so money creates קידושין and it belongs to the father.

steps.title: Why not give the money to the girl herself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the money should go to the girl, not her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the money goes to her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. Why should the father get the money and not the girl herself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The derivation showed that money is paid when she leaves her father's authority. It did not clearly prove who gets that money. Since she is the one getting married, maybe the money is hers.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (instead); introduces another possible reading
To her, to the girl herself

phrases.english: But say the money goes to her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 8 that the money belongs to the father.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'other master' who receives the money is the father.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The girl is the one being married, so the money could just as well be hers.

steps.title: The father gives her in marriage, so he takes the money
steps.stepSummary: The idea is rejected: the פסוק shows the father receives her קידושין, so it makes no sense for her to take the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you say that? Her father accepts her קידושין, as it is written: 'I gave my daughter to this man.' And she should take the money?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. The father is the one who accepts the קידושין, so the money is obviously his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'את בתי נתתי לאיש הזה' shows that the father is the one who marries off his daughter. If he is the one who does the transaction, it would be strange for her to keep the payment.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?! A strong way of saying the idea does not make sense
Accepts her קידושין
She takes the money

phrases.english: How can you say that?!
Her father accepts her קידושין,
as it is written: "I gave my daughter to this man",
and she should take the money?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Source-based rejection: a פסוק shows the father is the one who receives the קידושין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The money might belong to the girl, since she is the one being married.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father gives her in marriage, so the money is his.

steps.title: Maybe that is only true for a young girl, not an older one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the father's rights apply only to a קטנה, who cannot accept קידושין herself, but a נערה could betroth herself and keep the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say this applies only to a קטנה, who has no power to accept קידושין. But a נערה, who does have the power to accept קידושין, should be able to betroth herself and take the money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the last answer. Maybe the father gets the money only when his daughter is too young to act for herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's control was explained by his being the one who accepts the קידושין. A קטנה cannot accept קידושין herself, so it makes sense that her father does it. A נערה can accept קידושין on her own, so in her case the reason seems to fall away and the money could be hers.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl under twelve
A girl from twelve, for about six months, before she becomes fully grown
Literally 'hand': the legal power to make a transaction
She betroths herself

phrases.english: But say these words apply only to a minor girl,
who has no power to accept קידושין,
but a young woman (נערה),
phrases.notes: A נערה is a girl from age twelve, for about six months, before she becomes fully grown.

phrases.english: who does have the power to accept קידושין,
should betroth herself and take the money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer of Step 10 to a קטנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the father always gets the קידושין money because he is the one who accepts the קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reason fits only a girl who cannot act for herself. A נערה can accept קידושין on her own, so she should keep the money.

steps.title: All the profit of her youth goes to her father
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'בנעוריה בית אביה' teaches that everything a girl gains during her נערות belongs to her father.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'In her youth, in her father's house.' All the profit of her youth goes to her father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even a נערה's קידושין money goes to her father, because a פסוק gives him all the gains of her youth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's right does not depend only on his being the one who accepts the קידושין. The פסוק 'בנעוריה בית אביה' gives him all the gains of her youth. That includes the time she is a נערה, so her קידושין money is his.

keyTerms.meaning: In her youth, in her father's house
The profit or gain of her youth

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא learns from 'בנעוריה בית אביה' that even a נערה's קידושין money goes to her father. Watch this proof: in Step 15 the גמרא knocks it down, and in Step 19 it goes back to 'יצאה חנם אין כסף'.

phrases.english: The verse says: "In her youth, in her father's house"
All the profit of youth goes to her father.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New פסוק that covers the נערה as well.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נערה, who can accept קידושין herself, keeps her own קידושין money.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the gains of her youth, including a נערה's קידושין money, belong to her father.

steps.title: Then why does רב הונא need a different source for a daughter's earnings?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא learned that a daughter's earnings go to her father by comparing her to an אמה. The גמרא asks why he did not simply learn it from 'בנעוריה בית אביה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רב הונא's statement in the name of רב: From where do we know that a daughter's earnings belong to her father? From the פסוק 'And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.' Just as a maidservant's earnings go to her master, so too a daughter's earnings go to her father. Let him learn it from 'In her youth, in her father's house'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first quotes רב הונא's statement as a setup. Then it challenges him: the פסוק we just used already gives the father all the profit of her youth, so why did רב הונא need a different פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' means all the profit of her youth goes to her father, it should also cover her earnings from work. That would make רב הונא's comparison to an אמה unnecessary. Step 14 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But then; introduces a problem that follows from what was just said
From where (do we know)?
Her handiwork: the earnings from her work
Let him derive it (from another source)

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But then, what about that which Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
From where do we know that a daughter's earnings belong to the father?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכֹּר אִישׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה״,
phrases.english: For it says: "And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant",
just as a maidservant's earnings go to her master,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בַּת נָמֵי מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ לְאָבִיהָ.
phrases.english: so too a daughter's earnings go to her father.
Let him learn it from "In her youth, in her father's house"!
phrases.notes: This is the same פסוק the גמרא just used in Step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the source from Step 12 to challenge רב הונא's separate derivation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's derivation that a daughter's earnings go to her father, learned by comparing her to an אמה (שמות 21:7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' gives the father all the profit of her youth, it already covers her earnings, so רב הונא's separate source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רב הונא reads the פסוק as being only about vows
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא did not use 'בנעוריה בית אביה' for earnings, because he holds that this פסוק is written about הפרת נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that פסוק is written about cancelling vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. רב הונא did not use 'בנעוריה בית אביה' because he understands it as talking only about a father cancelling his daughter's vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בנעוריה בית אביה' come from the section of the תורה about vows. So רב הונא limits the פסוק to that subject, and it does not teach anything about money. That is why he needed the comparison to an אמה to learn about her earnings.

keyTerms.meaning: cancelling vows; a father can cancel the vows of his daughter while she is a נערה
that is written

phrases.english: Rather, about cancelling vows
phrases.notes: The פסוק 'בנעוריה בית אביה' is in במדבר 30:17, at the end of the section on vows.

phrases.english: is it written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 about רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the פסוק to one topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בנעוריה בית אביה' covers all of a נערה's gains, including her earnings.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רב הונא, 'בנעוריה בית אביה' speaks only about הפרת נדרים.

steps.title: Then the קידושין money is not covered by that פסוק either
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק is only about vows, then it also cannot teach that the father gets a נערה's קידושין money.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then also here (for קידושין money), it is written about cancelling vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns רב הונא's answer into a new problem. If 'בנעוריה בית אביה' is only about vows, then step 12's proof for the קידושין money of a נערה falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 used 'בנעוריה בית אביה' to show that a נערה's קידושין money goes to her father. If the פסוק is limited to vows, that proof no longer works. The question from step 11 comes back: maybe a נערה keeps her own קידושין money.

keyTerms.meaning: so too; the same applies here

phrases.english: So too, about cancelling vows
phrases.notes: He means: for קידושין money too, we should say the פסוק is only about vows.

phrases.english: is it written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, בַּהֲפָרַת נְדָרִים הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 14 to knock out the proof of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'בנעוריה בית אביה' (step 12) as the source for the father's right to a נערה's קידושין money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק is limited to vows for earnings, it must also be limited to vows for קידושין money.

steps.title: Money laws cannot be learned from vows
steps.stepSummary: One might suggest learning the father's money rights from his right over her vows, but money laws are not learned from prohibition laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us learn it from there (vows). We do not learn money matters from prohibition matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible way out. Someone might say we can learn from vows to money, but the גמרא rejects this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vows belong to איסור, laws of what is permitted and forbidden. The father's right to her money is ממון, a money matter. The rule is that we do not build a money law from an איסור law, so vows cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you would say; it introduces a suggestion that the גמרא is about to reject
let us learn it
money matters
prohibition matters; laws of what is forbidden or permitted

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn from it
phrases.notes: 'From it' means from the father's power to cancel her vows.

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from prohibition matters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the קשיא of step 15 by closing one escape route.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of learning a father's money rights from his right to cancel vows.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Money matters cannot be derived from איסור matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'ממונא מאיסורא לא ילפינן' is a basic rule about how laws are learned, and it comes up across ש״ס.

steps.title: Money laws cannot be learned from a fine
steps.stepSummary: One might suggest learning it from the קנס that is paid to the father, but money laws are not learned from fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us learn it from the fine. We do not learn money matters from a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a second possible source. The fine paid to the father of a נערה who was forced cannot serve as a source either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the קנס goes to the father. But a קנס is a special penalty, not a normal money law. So we cannot learn regular money rights, like קידושין money, from it.

keyTerms.meaning: a fine; a set penalty that the תורה requires, here paid to the father of a נערה who was forced
we learn

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn from a fine
phrases.notes: This is the fine of fifty silver coins paid to the girl's father, in דברים 22:29.

phrases.english: we do not learn money matters from a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a second escape route for the קשיא of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of learning the father's right from the קנס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A קנס is a special penalty, so regular money laws cannot be derived from it.

steps.title: Shame and damage payments are different
steps.stepSummary: One might suggest learning it from בושת ופגם, which go to the father, but those are different because the father himself has a share in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: let us learn it from shame and damage payments. Shame and damage are different, because her father has a connection to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a third possible source. The payments for her shame and damage cannot prove anything about her קידושין money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בושת ופגם are regular money payments, not a fine. But they are a special case, because the father has his own connection to them. He has the power to marry her off in a way that could shame or lower her, so these losses are partly his. That is not true of other money that comes to her.

keyTerms.meaning: payment for shame
payment for the loss in value; damage
it is different
has a share in it; is connected to it

phrases.english: And if you would say: let us learn from shame and damage payments
shame and damage are different
because her father has a share in them.
phrases.notes: He means the father could have caused this shame himself, for example by marrying her to a man with a skin disease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the third escape route, so the קשיא of step 15 stands.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of learning the father's right from בושת ופגם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The father has his own connection to her shame and damage, so this case cannot be applied to other money.
steps.whatToRemember: All three possible sources fail. Vows are איסור, a קנס is a special penalty, and in בושת ופגם the father has his own share. So the גמרא must find another way.

steps.title: Back to 'יצאה חנם אין כסף', with a logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the source 'יצאה חנם אין כסף' and begins a logical argument that the money goes to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it makes sense that when the פסוק excludes...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its final answer. It goes back to the original source and starts explaining, through logic, why the money belongs to the father and not to the girl. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other sources failed, so the גמרא returns to 'יצאה חנם אין כסף', which says there is no money for one master. Now it begins to answer the challenge from step 9, that the money might go to the girl. The idea is that when the פסוק takes money away from one owner, it makes sense that the money goes to the other owner, which is the father.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense; it is logical
excludes; leaves out

phrases.english: Rather, it makes sense
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means we go back to the first source, 'יצאה חנם אין כסף' in שמות 21:11.

phrases.english: that when it excludes

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the other sources are rejected, it goes back to the original פסוק and answers with logic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning based on what the פסוק excludes (the answer is still being built)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without 'בנעוריה בית אביה', maybe a נערה keeps her own קידושין money.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the פסוק excludes money from one master, logic says the money belongs to the other master, the father. The answer continues on the next amud.
